To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the freezing treatments of FW and DF affected the composition and colour of WFP prepared from haruan fish fillet.
freezing treatments affected the physicochemical properties and amino acid composition of whole fillet powder of snakehead fish.
freezing treatments affected the physicochemical properties and amino acid composition of WFPs from haruan fish.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation and characterization of fish WFP from snakehead fish.
the physicochemical properties and amino acid composition of WFPs from haruan fish fillets subjected to pre-filleting freeze treatments.
the physicochemical properties and amino acid composition of WFP prepared from snakehead fillets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of FW treatment in pre-filleting processing of haruan fish would be more suitable as it resulted in better yield and WFP with desirable physicochemical properties and amino acid composition.
freezing with distilled water is better than direct freezing for WFP preparation from snakehead fish.
the freezing treatments affected the colour of WFPs but did not influence their protein and moisture contents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
WFPFW was more acceptable in terms of its composition and physiochemical properties.
freezing of haruan fillets with distilled water (WFP-FW) was better for the production of WFP.
the freezing of fish fillet prior to fillet powder preparation could be an effective method to preserve the fillets and to produce a high quality WFP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
WFP can be produced from fillets obtained from haruan fish that were subjected to freezing with or without distilled water.
freezing of fish prior to filleting and subsequent preparation into WFPs can be done with distilled water or without water.
WFPFW is the best sample for further research and development.
